title: Physics (kinematics + mechanics)

grammar.note: Python module is the executable grammar source. Ranges verified: openwiki/architecture/physics-slice.md.

why_verify: Agents produce confident physics answers that sound right but silently break dimensional consistency, drop a stated quantity, or mis-derive a multi-step composition. Scoring cannot prove correctness; only constraint satisfaction plus trace can.
how_handled_now: Students/agents self-check and LLM-judges score plausibility. Both fail on the exact case that matters: an internally consistent but algebraically invalid derivation with no checkpoint.

roots: F = m*a treated as definitional relation in mechanics

scenarios.plain: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 4 m/s^2 for 10 s. Find the displacement.
Benchmark fixture — kinematics/mechanics composition (see RESULTS.md dyn-08).

benchmark.verdict_note: RESOLVED and answer within 1e-6 relative tolerance; UNKNOWN counts as fail.

verified.scope: core ontology, engine, layers, solvers, trace, physics-slice

decisions.title: Physics first as vertical slice
decisions.decision: Ship kinematics+mechanics deduction only; no legal/finance domains, no auto-extraction, no UI.
decisions.rationale: Prove the engine, dimension checking, and trace views on bounded, correct, testable slice before broad domains.

decisions.title: Velocity magnitude convention
decisions.decision: Multi-valued algebraic roots resolve to positive real (textbook magnitude).
decisions.rationale: Physics word problems expect magnitudes; the solve_symbolic backend applies this convention.

known_gaps: Z3 backend absent — physics is fully symbolic (sympy) today; discrete/threshold constraints not expressible.
Boundary case: kinematic regimes (v -> 0 stops) not modeled as discrete rules.
20-fixture benchmark is small; adversarial must-reject set not yet formalized (ARCHITECTURE.md section 9 question 2).

out_of_scope.claim: proof that all physics reduces to a universal root set
